name: Joiarib
overview: Joiarib was a male Levite known for his role as a teacher, specifically sent by Ezra to Iddo. As a member of the tribe of Levi, Joiarib held a position connected to religious instruction and leadership within the Israelite community. His mention is brief but highlights his function in supporting the spiritual restoration during Ezra's time.
namesAndTitles: The name Joiarib means 'y-h-v-h contends, pleads [your case],' reflecting a possible role of intercession or advocacy before God. This proper name, recorded in Ezra 8:16, is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance tied to divine contention or pleading.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Joiarib as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe responsible for temple duties and teaching. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Joiarib's significance lies in his role as a Levite teacher sent by Ezra, emphasizing the importance of religious education and leadership during the post-exilic period. His presence in Ezra 8:16 underscores the careful organization and spiritual renewal efforts led by Ezra among the returned exiles. Joiarib exemplifies the faithful Levites who supported the restoration of worship and adherence to God's law in Israel.
